title: Inference Practice 1
subject: rla
passage:
TEXT A - Extra Charger

Before a long meeting, Damon placed his laptop charger in his backpack and added a second charger. At the meeting room, he offered the extra one to a teammate whose battery warning had appeared.

TEXT B - Marked Map

A trail guide circled two bridges on a paper map and wrote "check after rain" beside both. After a storm, she visited those locations before inspecting the rest of the trail.

TEXT C - Priority Note

A desk note lists "call supplier," "finish poster," and "check room booking." The room-booking item is underlined twice. Five minutes later, Maya opens the booking website before touching the other tasks.

TEXT D - Window Seat

When the bus became crowded, Eli moved his bag from the seat beside him to the floor before anyone asked. He then shifted closer to the window and looked toward the aisle.

questions.prompt: What can the reader infer about Damon in Text A?
questions.explanation: Bringing a second charger and offering it when needed supports preparation for a possible need.
questions.rule: Choose what the clues support, not merely what could be true.

options.text: He anticipated that someone at the meeting might need charging help.
He expected the meeting to drain his own battery enough to require both chargers.
options.whyWrong: “He expected the meeting to drain his own battery enough to require both chargers.” may fit one clue, but it does not account for the full set of evidence.

options.text: He regularly lends electronic equipment to teammates at every meeting.
options.whyWrong: “He regularly lends electronic equipment to teammates at every meeting.” turns limited evidence into a broader rule than the text supports.

options.text: He knew before the meeting exactly which teammate would have a low battery.
options.whyWrong: “He knew before the meeting exactly which teammate would have a low battery.” is possible, but the passage does not provide enough evidence to justify it.

questions.prompt: Which detail best supports that inference?
questions.explanation: The extra charger is deliberate preparation beyond his own immediate need.
questions.rule: Choose what the clues support, not merely what could be true.

options.text: The meeting is described as long.
options.whyWrong: “The meeting is described as long.” is supported by only part of the evidence; another choice fits the whole pattern better.

options.text: A teammate’s battery warning appears in the meeting room.
options.whyWrong: “A teammate’s battery warning appears in the meeting room.” is supported by only part of the evidence; another choice fits the whole pattern better.

options.text: Damon packs a second charger before the meeting and later offers it when a teammate needs one.
Damon also packs a charger for his own laptop.
options.whyWrong: “Damon also packs a charger for his own laptop.” is supported by only part of the evidence; another choice fits the whole pattern better.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the two bridges in Text B?
questions.explanation: The note "check after rain" and first-priority inspection imply weather-related concern.
questions.rule: Choose what the clues support, not merely what could be true.

options.text: Rain may create problems at the two bridge locations.
The guide expects rain to affect only bridges and no other part of the trail.
options.whyWrong: “The guide expects rain to affect only bridges and no other part of the trail.” turns limited evidence into a broader rule than the text supports.

options.text: The bridges are unsafe after every storm.
options.whyWrong: “The bridges are unsafe after every storm.” is broader or more absolute than the passage supports.

options.text: The guide already knows exactly what kind of damage each bridge will have.
options.whyWrong: “The guide already knows exactly what kind of damage each bridge will have.” is possible, but the passage does not provide enough evidence to justify it.

questions.prompt: Which evidence most strongly supports the inference?
questions.explanation: The repeated emphasis and post-storm priority point directly to rain-related risk.
questions.rule: Choose what the clues support, not merely what could be true.

options.text: The map is made of paper rather than displayed on a phone.
options.whyWrong: “The map is made of paper rather than displayed on a phone.” is background information rather than the strongest evidence for the question.

options.text: The guide visits several locations on the trail.
options.whyWrong: “The guide visits several locations on the trail.” is supported by only part of the evidence; another choice fits the whole pattern better.

options.text: The two marked locations happen to be bridges.
options.whyWrong: “The two marked locations happen to be bridges.” is supported by only part of the evidence; another choice fits the whole pattern better.

options.text: The guide marks the bridges “check after rain” and inspects them before the rest of the trail after a storm.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the room booking in Text C?
questions.explanation: The double underline plus immediate action show priority.
questions.rule: Choose what the clues support, not merely what could be true.

options.text: Maya already knows the room is unavailable.
options.whyWrong: The passage does not support “Maya already knows the room is unavailable..” This adds a claim the text never establishes.

options.text: Maya treats the room booking as the most urgent task on the list.
Maya believes the other two tasks no longer need to be completed.
options.whyWrong: “Maya believes the other two tasks no longer need to be completed.” is broader or more absolute than the passage supports.

options.text: Maya can complete the room booking only by using a website.
options.whyWrong: “Maya can complete the room booking only by using a website.” is related to the passage, but it does not directly answer this question.

questions.prompt: Which detail best supports that inference?
questions.explanation: Both emphasis and action support urgency.
questions.rule: Choose what the clues support, not merely what could be true.

options.text: The note contains three separate tasks.
options.whyWrong: “The note contains three separate tasks.” is background information rather than the strongest evidence for the question.

options.text: “Call supplier” appears first on the written list.
options.whyWrong: ““Call supplier” appears first on the written list.” may fit one clue, but it does not account for the full set of evidence.

options.text: Maya underlines the booking item twice and opens the booking website before starting the other tasks.
Maya waits five minutes before opening the website.
options.whyWrong: “Maya waits five minutes before opening the website.” is supported by only part of the evidence; another choice fits the whole pattern better.

questions.prompt: What can the reader infer about Eli in Text D?
questions.explanation: Moving the bag from a seat as the bus crowds creates an open place for someone else.
questions.rule: Choose what the clues support, not merely what could be true.

options.text: Eli wants easier access to the aisle.
options.whyWrong: “Eli wants easier access to the aisle.” conflicts with a detail stated in the passage.

options.text: Eli expects to leave the bus at the next stop.
options.whyWrong: “Eli expects to leave the bus at the next stop.” predicts an outcome that the passage does not establish.

options.text: Eli is worried another passenger might touch his bag.
options.whyWrong: “Eli is worried another passenger might touch his bag.” assigns a motive that the text does not show through actions or wording.

options.text: Eli is making space so another passenger can use the seat beside him.

questions.prompt: Which detail most strongly supports the inference?
questions.explanation: The timing and action directly create an available seat.
questions.rule: Choose what the clues support, not merely what could be true.

options.text: The bus has become crowded.
options.whyWrong: “The bus has become crowded.” is supported by only part of the evidence; another choice fits the whole pattern better.

options.text: As the bus gets crowded, Eli moves his bag off the neighboring seat and onto the floor.
Eli looks toward the aisle after moving.
options.whyWrong: “Eli looks toward the aisle after moving.” is supported by only part of the evidence; another choice fits the whole pattern better.

options.text: Eli shifts closer to the window.
options.whyWrong: “Eli shifts closer to the window.” is supported by only part of the evidence; another choice fits the whole pattern better.

curriculum.learningObjective: Infer unstated ideas from multiple details and identify the strongest supporting evidence.
